Doctor corpus already encodes prose-to-command rows and controls

label: Four prompt corpora exist: 195 skill-level labeled rows, 66 holdout, 24 ambiguity, and 78 doctor rows whose expected_top is a command-bridge id.

Only the doctor slice asserts a command expectation, so command-level routing accuracy is measured for one of seven command families; the 195 skill rows carry skill_top_1 and skill_correct and no command field.

The doctor slice already tests the chat-only path: only 15 of 78 rows contain a literal /doctor, so 63 are prose prompts such as "Help me set up skilled", meaning the corpus shape the spec asks for exists but is scoped to one family.

Coverage is half-built inside that family: 17 of the 35 doctor bridges have at least one row and 18 have none, including the ci report/scaffold/toggle, overlay apply/repin/status, sk-code-quality, sk-skill check/convert, symlink link/unlink and four skill-advisor routes.

The slice carries 19 control rows whose expectation is a skill or null (create a git worktree to sk-git, review this pull request to sk-code, plus a null expectation), which is the wrongly-started guard already authored but doctor-scoped.

The captured baseline records only skill-level metrics (full_corpus_top1 158/195, unknown_count 13, gold_none_false_fire 5, holdout_top1 50/66, ambiguity_top1 20/24 at tau 0.03), so a change that made every command unrecommendable would leave the baseline green.

Four metrics separate the failure modes and two of them map onto existing names: command_recall as top-2 command accuracy and wrong_command_rate as the command analogue of gold_none_false_fire, plus policy_precision for run-or-ask and brief_naming to prove the rendered brief carries the command string.

Row budget for the remaining 28 commands is at least 56 positive and 28 control rows, and adding the 18 uncovered doctor bridges brings the command corpus to roughly 240 rows, the same order as the 195 skill rows already present.
Any command-surfacing change must be gated by a command-level metric, because the skill-level baseline cannot detect a command regression
